description: Generated from merge.cases.json by scripts/vectors.mjs using lib/merge-reference.mjs. Never hand-edit. Each case: merge(local, incoming) → expected {row, conflicts, outcome, write}, or expected {error} when the input is invalid (malformed_field_hlc | missing_column; every implementation must fail with the same code). Outcomes: inserted, inserted_deleted, updated, deleted, restored, unchanged. write = the merged row differs from local in any column. Frontiers (node → max HLC seen) default to the frontier of each side's own row (ADR 0017). "compaction" pins the generated x-compact placeholders.

cases.name: insert: row absent locally is inserted verbatim
identical rows: unchanged
incoming newer note wins; local was seen by the file → no conflict
local newer note kept against an old file → unchanged
AC-11.2: different groups edited on each side both survive
AC-11.3: same group edited on both sides, incoming later wins, local value logged
AC-11.3: same group edited on both sides, local later wins, incoming value logged
ADR 0017: incoming edit made after seeing ours is an update, not a conflict
equal values with different stamps: newer stamp kept, no conflict
amount group moves together (amount + currency + original)
incoming tombstone deletes a live row
AC-11.4: later field edit never resurrects a deleted row
AC-11.4: an old file never resurrects a deletion
restore (newer deleted-group write with null) brings the row back
delete after a concurrent restore stays deleted; restore logged
group missing in the file's field_hlc counts as '' → local wins
group missing locally → incoming wins
tie (same stamp, different values) → larger value wins (direction 1)
tie (same stamp, different values) → larger value wins (direction 2)
tie order: null < integer < string
HLC counter orders edits within the same millisecond
created_at keeps the minimum, updated_at the maximum
several groups at once: mixed winners
ledger entry: amount edit on one side, note on the other
transaction_tags: removing a tag (tombstone) merges; file frontier covers our stamp → no conflict
transaction_tags: re-adding after removal on the other side (restore wins by HLC)
error: field_hlc with whitespace is malformed
error: field_hlc stamp with non-hex node is malformed
error: field_hlc stamp that is not an HLC ("9") is malformed
error: empty-string field_hlc is malformed (only {} is empty)
error: field_hlc that is not a string is malformed
error: field_hlc with a trailing newline is malformed
error: uppercase hex in a stamp is malformed
error: group name with capitals is malformed
error: short wall clock in a stamp is malformed
error: malformed local field_hlc is rejected too
error: malformed incoming field_hlc is rejected even when the row is new
error: incoming row missing a column
error: local row missing a column (field_hlc itself)
error: new row missing a column
error: a missing column is reported before a malformed field_hlc
valid: {} is an empty field_hlc; every group counts as "" so local wins
unknown groups (incl. one named "constructor") keep the max stamp on both sides, values untouched
unknown group "constructor" present only in the file is adopted
unknown group present only locally is kept; nothing to write
immutable columns that differ: the larger value wins (source manual vs sms → sms), no conflict
immutable columns that differ: same result in the other direction
immutable on a system row: null loses to a value (tags.system_key)
external_ref is LWW: a re-parse with a newer stamp corrects it
external_ref edited on both sides: later stamp wins, losing ref logged
seed-like: equal values, newer stamps and earlier created_at → unchanged but write
tombstone for a row we never had → inserted_deleted
both sides deleted with different deleted_at → unchanged value-wise, but write
only stamps differ (no value change): unchanged, write
compacted tombstone beats an older full row and never resurrects (file side)
compacted tombstone beats an older full row and never resurrects (local side)
compacted tombstone whose older rival edit was unseen: the lost edit is logged
compaction keeps NOT NULL foreign keys (ledger_entries.person_id)
